summary: Root cause identified with high confidence (0.82): the portfolio-page timeouts and gateway p99/504 spikes were caused by config change cfg-2207, which shrank portfolio-service's db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z, saturating the connection pool and cascading upstream timeouts to api-gateway. The evidence chain is complete at every hop: a change inventory with exactly three items (F1/F13), the pool pinned flat at its new ceiling of 5.0 with flat CPU (F12), HikariPool total=5/active=5/idle=0/waiting=43 with "could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms" (F11), simultaneous portfolio-service and gateway latency/error steps (F7/F8/F10), and 252/255 gateway WARNs being upstream timeouts to portfolio-service (F9). The reporter's gateway HTTP/2 upgrade hypothesis (H2) is affirmatively contradicted on timing (1h52m quiet gap before onset), mechanism (an envoy/stream-layer fault cannot pin a Hikari pool at exactly 5), and scope (order-service, the other service that upgrade touched, stayed healthy). The gateway is a symptom carrier, not the origin. The one caveat keeping this inferential rather than confirmed is that neither suspect was ever reverted, so the decisive revert-and-recover test does not exist in the data.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service DB pool shrunk to 5 by cfg-2207, saturating the pool and cascading 504s to gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-2207 on portfolio-service reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource', author infra-automation). Normal portfolio-page concurrency needs more than 5 concurrent connections (baseline in-use ~11.4-13.3), so the pool pins at its ceiling (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiters=43). Requests block ~3000ms trying to acquire a JDBC connection and then fail; portfolio-service latency/errors spike, api-gateway's upstream calls to portfolio-service time out (504), inflating gateway p99. The gateway is a symptom carrier, not the origin.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 lands on portfolio-service at 09:52:00Z reducing db.pool.max_size 50->5
Pool pins at its new ceiling 5: db_pool_in_use falls from ~12 to a flat 5.0 while cpu_pct stays flat ~35-36%, i.e. ceiling not load
Requests queue for JDBC connections; HikariPool reports total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43 and 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' from 09:53:19Z
portfolio-service p99 jumps from 176ms to ~1865-4546ms and error rate to ~22% in the 09:50-09:55 bucket

api-gateway upstream calls to portfolio-service time out: 252/255 gateway WARNs are 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' from 09:53:53Z, gateway p99 steps to ~1850-4400ms and error rate to ~7%

Fault is localized to the portfolio path: all other ledger-db consumers (order, payment, settlement) and the other HTTP/2-upgraded dependency (order-service) stay flat at 09:50-09:55Z, and ledger-db's own query/CPU load is flat

assumptions: Normal portfolio-page concurrency at 09:52Z required more than 5 concurrent DB connections: implied by the pre-change baseline db_pool_in_use ~11.4-13.3 but not verified against request-rate/queueing data at that instant (critic minor point).

Ther residual possibility that a downstream ledger-db slowdown (rather than the 5-connection ceiling per se) holds the connections: ledger-db slow_queries_per_min and cpu_pct are flat (F28), but connections_active and replication_lag_ms were never retrieved, so a connection-level DB stall is not formally excluded. Even so, a DB-side stall would be expected to hit the other ledger-db consumers, which it did not (F26,F27,F29).
No revert of cfg-2207 exists up to latest data, so the decisive revert-and-recover test remains unperformed (F18,F22,F23); attribution stays timing+mechanism inferential.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220) broke upstream connection handling (reporter's hypothesis)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-5220 upgraded envoy 1.29->1.30 and enabled HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service at 08:00Z. The reporter suspects a regression in upstream connection/stream handling (e.g. changed HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams default, as in HIST-116), producing gateway upstream timeouts and 504s on the portfolio path. May be causal or merely amplifier.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 enables HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service upstreams at 08:00:00Z
Envoy HTTP/2 default change degrades upstream stream handling, stalling portfolio-path requests at the proxy layer

assumptions: The upgrade ran quietly for ~1h52m (08:00Z -> 09:52Z) before any impact, with no ramp at 08:00Z — a long, unexplained lag after the change.
A contributing/amplifying role (not origin) cannot be fully excluded because no envoy max-concurrent-streams state or gateway stream/concurrency telemetry was retrieved.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted on timing, mechanism and scope. (a) Timing: dep-5220 landed 08:00Z but latency/errors stepped abruptly at 09:50-09:53Z with no ramp at 08:00Z (F7,F14) — a ~1h52m quiet gap. (b) Mechanism: the concrete failure is inside portfolio-service (HikariPool total=5, active=5, idle=0; F11,F12), not at the envoy/stream layer; HTTP/2 stream starvation would not pin a Hikari pool at exactly the cfg-2207 ceiling of 5 (F17). (c) Scope: order-service, the OTHER service targeted by the same HTTP/2 change, shows no step at 09:50-09:55Z in either latency (F24, max ~163ms) or error rate (F25, 0.10-0.32%); the change therefore demonstrably did not degrade the second service it touched. cfg-2207 landed within ~1 minute of onset (F14).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared datastore/cache (ledger-db or redis-cache) degraded, inflating portfolio-path latency
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared dependency used by portfolio-service (ledger-db postgres shared=true, or redis-cache shared=true) degraded or failed over (as in HIST-102's ledger-db failover), making portfolio-service DB/cache calls slow, exhausting its connection pool and inflating gateway p99. The 5-connection ceiling could then be starved by a downstream stall rather than being the cause.

causal_chain.claim: Shared ledger-db/redis-cache slows or fails over, or ledger-db connections saturate
portfolio-service queries block, holding each of its few connections
portfolio-service Hikari pool exhausts (total=5, active=5, idle=0) and latency/errors spike
Gateway times out on portfolio path, 504s

assumptions: An infrastructure-level event on ledger-db/redis-cache occurred but is absent from the change inventory (which by the team's own note does not cover infra failovers).
ledger-db connections_active/replication_lag_ms and redis-cache hit_ratio_pct/cpu were never retrieved, so a connection-level ($not lazy-load) DB or cache stall is not formally excluded.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Now contradicted by the negative controls the critic asked for, not merely dismissed. (a) Scope: ledger-db is shared by order-service, payment-service and settlement-service (F5,F15); all three stay flat across 09:50-09:55Z — order latency <=163ms and errors 0.1-0.32% (F24,F25), payment p99 299-340ms (F26), settlement p99 212-250ms (F27). (b) Mechanism: ledger-db's own slow_queries_per_min (~1/min) and cpu_pct (~30%) are flat across 08:00-10:05Z with no step at 09:52Z (F28,F29). A shared-DB origin is thus affirmatively contradicted rather than unverified. (c) Residual: connections_active and redis metrics were never retrieved, and no infra failover appears in change history, so the mechanism cannot be positively cited.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Coincidental/no faulty change — traffic growth or noisy neighbor exhausting provisioned capacity
ranked_hypotheses.statement: No single change caused the fault; coincident traffic growth or a noisy neighbor pushed api-gateway/portfolio-service past provisioned capacity at 09:52Z, producing timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: Traffic rises above provisioned capacity around 09:52Z
Portfolio-service pool saturates and gateway times out

assumptions: Unrecorded traffic spike or noisy neighbor at ~09:52Z.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The pool is pinned at a hard ceiling of exactly 5 (F12), which is the value just set by cfg-2207 (F1,F3,F13); CPU stayed flat ~35% (F12) and the change inventory is complete with exactly one deployment and two config changes (F13), leaving no room for an invisible capacity event. cfg-2207 landing 09:52:00Z, ~1 minute before first errors (F14), explains the data far better.

facts.statement: The complete change inventory for 00:00-11:59Z across all services contains exactly three items: deployment dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, 08:00:00Z, envoy 1.29->1.30 plus HTTP/2 to upstreams, status live, never rolled back), config cfg-2199 (order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2, 07:00:00Z), and config cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5, 09:52:00Z, author infra-automation).
cfg-2207 reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource'), and this change is not mentioned in the incident report.

Temporal ordering is tight: cfg-2207 landed at 09:52:00Z, within ~1 minute of the first portfolio-service JDBC-acquire error at 09:53:19Z and the first gateway 504 at 09:53:53Z, whereas the gateway upgrade dep-5220 landed 1h52m earlier at 08:00Z with no rollback.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use fell from a ~11.4-13.3 connection baseline to a flat 5.0 from 09:55Z onward while its cpu_pct stayed flat at ~35-36%, i.e. the pool is pinned at its ceiling with no CPU pressure.

portfolio-service logs show JDBC connection-pool exhaustion: 270 events 'GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (first_seen 09:53:19Z) and 233 HikariPool events such as 'total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43'.
api-gateway latency_p99_ms stepped abruptly from a ~200ms baseline (09:45 avg 204.03ms) to avg 1849.99ms/max 4418.76ms in the 09:50 bucket with no gradual ramp, holding ~4200-4400ms through 11:55Z.
api-gateway error_rate stepped in the same 09:50 bucket from ~0.2% baseline to avg 1.66%/max 7.18%, then ~7.1-7.3% thereafter.

Gateway error logs are dominated by upstream timeouts to portfolio-service: 252 of 255 WARNs match 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings -> <n>', first entry 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' at 09:53:53Z.

Downstream portfolio-service stepped at the same moment as the gateway: latency_p99_ms rose from 176.42ms avg at 09:45 to avg 1865.15ms/max 4546.3ms at 09:50 (holding ~4100-4300ms), and error_rate rose from 0.18% at 09:45 to avg 4.65%/max 22.3% at 09:50 then ~22%.
Negative control: order-service, the other service targeted by dep-5220's HTTP/2 change, shows no step at 09:50-09:55Z — p99 stays within 139.34-162.83ms and error rate within 0.10-0.32%.

Negative control: the other ledger-db consumers show no step at 09:50-09:55Z — payment-service p99 stays in 299.45-340.3ms and settlement-service p99 in 211.65-249.93ms — while ledger-db is shared by order-, portfolio-, payment- and settlement-service.
Shared component ledger-db was normal across 08:00-10:05Z: slow_queries_per_min flat at ~1/min and cpu_pct flat at ~30%, with no step at 09:50-09:55Z.

No revert of either suspect occurred: portfolio-service's live db.pool.max_size remains 5 (old_value 50) from 09:52:00Z, config changes across all services in 11:00-11:59Z number 0, dep-5220 remains status live with rolled_back_at null, and portfolio-service had no deployment in the window — so there is no revert-and-recover event and the decisive causal test was never run.

The portfolio path topology is api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http) -> ledger-db (db), redis-cache (cache), market-data-service (http); the only datastore-driven shared components are ledger-db (shared=true) and redis-cache (shared=true), so a shared-component common cause would also hit other consumers, not just the portfolio page.

Mechanism comparison with precedent favours the config-change pattern: the observed failure is a fixed connection-pool ceiling (total=5, active=5, idle=0 with waiters) producing 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (matching HIST-115's pool-size config regression), whereas the envoy HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams precedent (HIST-116) would starve streams at the proxy layer and would not produce a portfolio-service HikariPool with total=5.

The negative-control result localizes the fault: the other ledger-db consumers are flat/healthy at 09:50-09:55Z and ledger-db's own query/CPU load is flat, so a shared-DB origin is contradicted and the fault is localized to the portfolio-service path — consistent with cfg-2207's scope.

assumptions: Normal portfolio-page concurrency at 09:52Z required more than 5 concurrent DB connections: this is implied by the pre-change baseline db_pool_in_use of ~11.4-13.3 but was not directly verified against request-rate/queueing data at that instant (critic's minor point).

The residual possibility that a downstream ledger-db slowdown (rather than the 5-connection ceiling per se) is what held the connections cannot be formally excluded, because ledger-db connections_active and replication_lag_ms were never retrieved; however a DB-side stall would be expected to hit the other ledger-db consumers, which it did not (F26/F27/F29).

Because no revert of cfg-2207 exists up to the latest data (F18/F22/F23), the decisive revert-and-recover test remains unperformed; the attribution therefore rests on timing plus mechanism and stays inferential rather than experimentally confirmed.

The 'config value is still 5' conclusion is inferred from the absence of any subsequent change record, not from a direct effective-value read; a small residual risk remains that an out-of-band revert exists that is not recorded in change history.

The claim that the HTTP/2 upgrade is inert for these symptoms rests on timing and mechanism mismatch (and on order-service's non-impact), not on direct envoy stream/concurrency telemetry or envoy configuration state, which was never retrieved.

timeline.event: Deployment dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0) goes live: envoy 1.29->1.30 and upstream protocol h2 enabled for portfolio-service and order-service. No impact follows — a 1h52m quiet gap before onset.
Pre-onset baseline: api-gateway p99 avg 204.03ms, portfolio-service p99 avg 176.42ms / error_rate 0.18%, order-service p99 139.34-156.5ms, ledger-db slow_queries ~1/min and CPU ~30%.

Abrupt step with no ramp in the 09:50 bucket: api-gateway p99 avg 1849.99ms / max 4418.76ms and error_rate avg 1.66% / max 7.18%; portfolio-service p99 avg 1865.15ms / max 4546.3ms and error_rate avg 4.65% / max 22.3%.

Config change cfg-2207 applied on portfolio-service: db.pool.max_size reduced 50 -> 5 ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource', author infra-automation). This is the only config change on the affected service and is not mentioned in the incident report.

First portfolio-service JDBC error: 'GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms'; 270 such events and 233 HikariPool exhaustion events (e.g. total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43).
First gateway upstream timeout to portfolio-service: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504 (trace 4ad3127e)'; 252 of 255 gateway WARNs are this pattern.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use settles at a flat 5.0 (down from ~11.4-13.3 baseline) while cpu_pct stays flat at ~35-36% — the pool is pinned at its new ceiling with no CPU pressure.
Incident INC-002 reported by on-call SRE; symptoms recorded as api-gateway p99 > 4s and 504s on /v1/portfolio/*, with the gateway HTTP/2 upgrade suspected.
Symptoms persist: api-gateway p99 held ~4200-4400ms and error rate ~7.1-7.3%; the fault is sustained, not transient.

Latest data: neither suspect was removed — cfg-2207 remains in effect (db.pool.max_size=5, zero config changes across all services 11:00-11:59Z), dep-5220 remains live with rolled_back_at null, and portfolio-service had no deployment in the window. No revert-and-recover signal exists.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately revert config change cfg-2207 on portfolio-service: restore db.pool.max_size from 5 back to 50 (the pre-change value; equivalent to rolling back the 'cost-optimisation profile small' datasource override). Watch portfolio-service db_pool_in_use/active/idle/waiting and 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' log rate, plus api-gateway p99 and 504 rate, within the first 5 minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the diagnosed origin: the pool pins at exactly the ceiling cfg-2207 set (F12), requests time out acquiring connections (F11), and gateway 504s follow within ~1 minute of the change (F9/F14). Reverting is also the decisive causal test that has never been run (F18/F22/F23) — recovery after revert would confirm the attribution experimentally.

recommended_actions.action: Do not roll back dep-5220 (the gateway HTTP/2 upgrade) as a first move: hold it as a fallback only if the cfg-2207 revert does not restore gateway p99/504s within a few minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is affirmatively contradicted on timing (1h52m quiet gap between 08:00Z deploy and 09:50Z onset), mechanism (an envoy/stream-layer fault cannot pin a Hikari pool at exactly 5), and scope (order-service, the other HTTP/2-upgraded service, stayed flat) (F7/F14/F24/F25/F17/F2). Rolling back an uninvolved change would destroy the clean revert-and-recover test for H1 and add risk.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery with before/after evidence: compare portfolio-service and api-gateway p99, error rate/504 count, and db_pool_in_use against the pre-onset baseline (gateway p99 ~204ms, portfolio p99 ~176ms, pool ~11.4-13.3) over the 10 minutes after the revert, and confirm the HikariPool waiting/acquire-timeout events stop.
recommended_actions.rationale: The outstanding causal test is revert-and-recover; only post-revert metric movement can upgrade the current inferential attribution to confirmed (F22, F18). Baseline values are established by F7, F10 and F12.

recommended_actions.action: Right-size the portfolio-service connection pool explicitly: set db.pool.max_size based on measured peak concurrent demand (baseline in-use was ~11.4-13.3 with 43 waiters under the 5-connection ceiling), rather than inheriting it from a 'small' cost-optimisation profile; if the intent was cost reduction, apply it to a non-prod profile only.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 50->5 shrink was below normal operating demand for this page, which is what produced the sustained saturation (F3, F12, F11). This prevents the cost-optimisation profile from being re-applied unchanged.

recommended_actions.action: Add a pre-apply guardrail to the infra-automation config pipeline that rejects or requires approval for changes to datasource pool sizing on services whose observed db_pool_in_use peak exceeds the new value (portfolio-service peak ~13.3 vs proposed 5), and add a pool-saturation alert on db_pool_in_use at/near max_size plus waiting-connection count.
recommended_actions.rationale: The change was applied by automation with no validation of live demand and was not rolled back for over two hours (F3, F18, F19); the historic analogue HIST-115 ('Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile') was closed by 'Reverted config; added validation' (F16, F23). Detection would also have shortened time-to-mitigation.

recommended_actions.action: Correct the incident record: mark the gateway HTTP/2 upgrade dep-5220 as investigated-and-excluded and record cfg-2207 as the root cause, so the reporter's initial suspicion does not persist in postmortem follow-up.
recommended_actions.rationale: The reported trigger (dep-5220) is contradicted on timing, mechanism and scope (F7, F14, F17, F24, F25), while cfg-2207 was absent from the report entirely (F3); the record should reflect the evidence.

data_gaps: No revert of cfg-2207 (or dep-5220) occurred up to the latest data (F18, F19, F20, F21, F22), so the decisive revert-and-recover causal test does not exist and cannot be reconstructed from existing data — the attribution is timing+mechanism inferential rather than experimentally confirmed. This is the single largest limitation on the conclusion.

redis-cache metrics were never successfully retrieved (hit_rate query returned not_found; the corrected hit_ratio_pct re-query hit the tool-call budget), so the redis half of the shared-component check is unanswered — though a redis-wide stall would also have hit other redis consumers.

ledger-db connections_active and replication_lag_ms were not retrieved, so a connection-level (rather than query/CPU-level) DB stall at 09:50-09:55Z cannot be formally excluded; its slow_queries_per_min and cpu_pct were flat (F28), which makes this unlikely.

payment-service and settlement-service error_rate were not retrieved (budget exhausted) — only their p99 latency was obtained, so the error-rate negative control for two of the three other ledger-db consumers is missing.

No gateway-side envoy stream/concurrency telemetry or max-concurrent-streams configuration was retrieved, so a contributing (non-causal) amplifier role for dep-5220 cannot be positively excluded; the exclusion rests on timing, mechanism mismatch and order-service non-impact.

The change inventory does not cover infrastructure-level events on ledger-db/redis-cache (e.g. failover, volume throttling), so an infra event like HIST-102's ledger-db failover cannot be confirmed or excluded from change history alone.

Metric buckets are 300s wide, so sub-minute onset ordering could only be bounded to the 09:50-09:55 bucket; earliest log evidence is 09:53:19Z (portfolio-service) vs 09:53:53Z (gateway 504) — a 34s gap — so whether pool exhaustion strictly preceded the gateway 504s is only established at bucket granularity.

The current effective value of db.pool.max_size is inferred from the absence of any subsequent change record rather than read directly, leaving a small residual risk of an unrecorded out-of-band revert.
api-gateway cpu_pct/memory_pct and portfolio-service restarts/memory were not queried (budget exhausted), so gateway resource saturation and blast radius beyond the portfolio path remain unverified.
HIST-115/HIST-116 were retrieved via search fields only (title/symptoms/root_cause), so their exact onset-vs-change offsets could not be compared against this incident.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Reverting cfg-2207 (restoring db.pool.max_size to 50) fails to restore portfolio-service p99, HikariPool availability and gateway 504 rate — that would falsify H1 as the origin and re-open the gateway upgrade and shared-dependency hypotheses.

Retrieval of ledger-db connections_active and replication_lag_ms showing a connection-level stall (or redis-cache hit_ratio_pct collapse) beginning at ~09:50-09:55Z while the other consumers were unaffected — this would suggest connections were held by a downstream stall rather than the 5-connection ceiling and would reopen H3.

Evidence that the other HTTP/2-upgraded dependency (order-service) and/or the other ledger-db consumers (payment-, settlement-service) did step at 09:50-09:55Z in metrics not yet retrieved (e.g. their error_rate), which would widen the blast radius and contradict the localization to the portfolio path.

Direct envoy telemetry showing max-concurrent-streams exhaustion or stream resets on the portfolio upstream coincident with onset, which would establish dep-5220 as a contributing amplifier (or alternative cause) rather than inert.

Evidence of an unrecorded out-of-band revert or of a second config/deploy change in the window (e.g. infrastructure-level ledger-db/redis-cache event) that the change inventory does not cover, which would break the 'exactly three changes, one on the affected service' basis of the attribution.

Evidence that normal portfolio-page concurrency at 09:52Z was in fact below 5 database connections (e.g. request-rate/queueing data showing the baseline 11.4-13.3 in-use figure was not load-driven), which would undercut the claim that the new ceiling was too low.

Shared components that could be a COMMON cause: ledger-db (type postgres, shared=true) is used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service; redis-cache (type redis, shared=true) is used by portfolio-service, market-data-service and auth-service. api-gateway itself is not shared and all path services have_telemetry=true; external bank-partner-api and kyc-provider have_telemetry=false.

Ordering: the gateway upgrade dep-5220 landed 1h52m before onset (08:00Z vs onset ~09:52-09:53Z) with no rollback, whereas cfg-2207 landed at 09:52:00Z on portfolio-service — the same service and same request path as the fault — within ~1 minute of the reporting times (portfolio-service first JDBC-acquire error 09:53:19Z, first gateway 504 at 09:53:53Z).

Dependency map confirms portfolio-service sits directly on the fault path behind api-gateway (api-gateway -> portfolio-service, kind http) and that the only datastore-driven shared components are ledger-db (postgres, shared=true, used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service) and redis-cache (redis, shared=true) — so a shared-component common cause (e.g. ledger-db failover, cache storm) would also hit order-service/payment-service, not just the portfolio page.

Historical precedent is split between the two candidate mechanisms for these exact symptoms: HIST-116 (2025-12-18, category bad_deployment) 'HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade', root_cause 'Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default', resolution 'Rolled back gateway' — and HIST-115 (2025-09-25, category config_change) 'connection pool misconfiguration' with root_cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', resolution 'Reverted config; added validation'. HIST-102 (2025-09-02) also produced portfolio page timeouts/504 at gateway via an unrelated ledger-db primary failover.

findings.statement: Mechanism comparison favours the config-change precedent: the observed failure is a fixed connection-pool ceiling (total=5, active=5, idle=0 with waiters) producing 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' — the exact pattern of HIST-115's pool-size config regression — whereas envoy HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams precedent (HIST-116) would starve streams at the gateway/proxy layer and not produce a portfolio-service HikariPool with total=5.

findings.statement: No revert of cfg-2207: portfolio-service is the ONLY config change in the window and its live value remains db.pool.max_size new_value=5 (old_value 50) from 09:52:00Z. The change is still in effect.
No removal-of-suspect action in the most recent hour either: config changes across ALL services between 11:00:00Z and 11:59:00Z (latest data) return count 0.
The gateway upgrade dep-5220 was also never rolled back: it remains status 'live' with rolled_back_at null as of latest data, and api-gateway has 0 config changes in 09:00-11:59Z.
No deployment of any kind on portfolio-service in the window (count 0), so no code-level revert there either.

Because neither suspect (cfg-2207 config nor dep-5220 deployment) was removed at any point up to latest data, there is no revert-and-recover event: the decisive causal test for H1 cannot be run with existing data, and the config attribution stays inferential (timing + mechanism) rather than confirmed.

Precedent structure matches the un-reverted pattern: HIST-115 was a pool-size config regression resolved by 'Reverted config; added validation'; HIST-116 was a gateway upgrade resolved by 'Rolled back gateway' — both prior incidents reached resolution via an explicit removal action, absent here.
